rationale: The data processing inequality states that downstream processing cannot increase information about an upstream variable. In the cognitive setting, the representation i is derived from sensory data caused by O, so any internal comparison using i cannot add information about O beyond what the sensory channel already provided. This supports the claim that the system cannot independently confirm representational accuracy, though the principle is about confirmation and access rather than information quantity.
